messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: [stan-users] JAGS to RStan
parts:
Hi Katie,

I haven't had a chance to get into your model, but the error is coming from near the start of your model block within the Stan program. You've defined a local variable muraw, then use it before setting it to anything sensible. Local variables in Stan are initialized to NaN (not a number). In Windows, that gets printed out as "1.#QNAN".

It looks like you're wanting to initialize it (from the R script). Perhaps you meant to declare muraw as a parameter?



Daniel

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] JAGS to RStan
parts:
Same problem. Stan code is executed in order and variables
must be defined before they are used.

It looks like you also have an indexing problem.

model {
...
matrix[nsites,nspecies] Mu;
...
for(species in 1:nspecies) {
for(k in 1:K) {
Betaraw[species,k] ~ normal(muraw[k], tau[k]);
}
}

for (sites in 1:nsites) {
for (species in 1:nspecies) {
Mu[species, sites] <- dot_product(Betaraw[species], X[sites]);
Z[sites] ~ multi_normal(Mu[sites], Tau);

1. You need to define the relevant parts of Mu before you use it.
You haven't, which is why you're getting NaN errors.

2. The second problem is that you use Mu[sites], which is indexed
the wrong way around compared to how Mu[species,sites] is defined.
Mu[sites] is the row with index sites out of Mu. You can extract
the column with col(Mu,sites).

But what you really want to do is just set up your Betaraw and
X appropriately so that you can do a matrix product and then
vectorize multi_normal. We can help you with that if you get the
basic model working first. Otherwise, I'd just be guessing.

- Bob
